title: Bio-SAXS of single-stranded DNA-binding proteins: radiation protection by the compatible solute ectoine.
authors: Hallier, Dorothea C; Smales, Glen J; Seitz, Harald; Hahn, Marc Benjamin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SAXS测量中单链DNA结合蛋白G5P的辐射保护，涉及蛋白-DNA互作体系但聚焦辐射损伤与保护剂效应，方法含蒙特卡洛模拟但非TF-DNA结合机制建模，相关性有限。
abstract: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) can be used for structural determination of biological macromolecules and polymers in their native states (e.g. liquid phase). This means that the structural changes of (bio-)polymers, such as proteins and DNA, can be monitored in situ to understand their sensitivity to changes in chemical environments. In an attempt to improve the reliability of such experiments, the reduction of radiation damage occurring from exposure to X-rays is required. One such method, is to use scavenger molecules to protect macromolecules against radicals produced during radiation exposure, such as reactive oxygen species (ROS). In this study we investigate the feasibility of applying the compatible solute, osmolyte and radiation protector Ectoine (THP(B)), as a scavenger molecule during SAXS measurements of the single-stranded DNA-binding protein Gene-V Protein (G5P/GVP). In this case, we monitor the radiation induced changes of G5P during bio-SAXS measurments and the resulting microscopic energy-damage relation was determined from microdosimetric calculations by Monte-Carlo based particle scattering simulations with TOPAS/Geant4 and a custom target-model. This resulted in a median-lethal energy deposit of pure G5P at 4 mg mL(-1) of E(1/2) = 7 +/- 5 eV, whereas a threefold increase of energy-deposit was needed under the presence of Ectoine to reach the same level of damage. This indicates that Ectoine increases the possible exposure time before radiation-damage to G5P is observed. Furthermore, the dominant type of damage shifted from aggregation in pure solutions towards a fragmentation for solutions containing Ectoine as a cosolute. These results are interpreted in terms of indirect radiation damage by reactive secondary species, as well as post-irradiation effects, related to preferential-exclusion of the cosolute from the protein surface. Hence, Ectoine is shown to provide a non-disturbing way to improve structure-determination of proteins via bio-SAXS in future studies.
abstract_zh: 小角X射线散射（SAXS）可用于生物大分子和聚合物在其天然状态（如液相）下的结构测定。这意味着，诸如蛋白质和DNA等（生物）聚合物的结构变化可以原位监测，以理解其对化学环境变化的敏感性。为了提高此类实验的可靠性，需要减少X射线照射引起的辐射损伤。一种方法是使用清除剂分子来保护大分子免受辐射暴露期间产生的自由基（如活性氧物种（ROS））的侵害。在本研究中，我们探讨了在单链DNA结合蛋白基因V蛋白（G5P/GVP）的SAXS测量中，应用相容性溶质、渗透调节剂和辐射保护剂Ectoine（THP(B)）作为清除剂分子的可行性。在此情况下，我们监测了生物SAXS测量期间G5P的辐射诱导变化，并通过基于蒙特卡洛的粒子散射模拟（使用TOPAS/Geant4和自定义靶模型）进行微剂量学计算，确定了由此产生的微观能量-损伤关系。结果显示，纯G5P在4 mg mL(-1)浓度下的中位致死能量沉积为E(1/2) = 7 ± 5 eV，而在Ectoine存在下，达到相同损伤水平所需的能量沉积增加了三倍。这表明Ectoine延长了在观察到G5P辐射损伤之前的可能暴露时间。此外，主要损伤类型从纯溶液中的聚集转变为含有Ectoine作为共溶质的溶液中的碎片化。这些结果被解释为反应性次级物种引起的间接辐射损伤，以及共溶质从蛋白质表面优先排斥相关的辐照后效应。因此，Ectoine被证明提供了一种非干扰性的方式，可在未来的生物SAXS研究中改善蛋白质的结构测定。
